title: Random forest derives an abbreviated three-item smell test for Parkinson disease
summary: Random forests trained on Sniffin' Stick data from 890 people with Parkinson disease and 313 controls ranked the 16 odors; a 3-stick model (anise, licorice, banana) separated poor from good smell ability with AUC 0.95 in the development set. Internal and external validation gave AUCs of at least 0.90, tested in a second PD dataset (n=452) and two REM sleep behavior disorder datasets (n=241 and n=37). The combined iRBD screen had 65% sensitivity and 30% negative predictive value.
ai_technology: Random forest feature ranking of Sniffin' Stick odor items used to derive a 3-stick abbreviated olfaction test
organization: University of Oxford; University of Bristol; Philipps University Marburg; Queen Elizabeth University Hospital Glasgow

evidence.tested: Internal validation plus independent PD (n=452) and iRBD (n=241, n=37) datasets; existing data.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical use as a screen and its predictive value for conversion in prodromal disease; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Ranks odor-identification items and defines a short test that approximates the full 16-item result.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
